title: Just A Game Engine
author: Sure_Excuse_8824
selftext:
I’m building a game engine called “Just A Game Engine” designed for storytellers, writers, tabletop gamers, and other creatives who don't know how to code. The goal is to provide a way for people to build their vision the way they imagined it instead of a pre-baked template with their art and ideas  slapped over it, reduced to fit the tool until it's barely recognizable . This is not a magic box. It’s not meant to be some one hour to demo toy. It will take real work. I estimate once ready for the public, it would take at least a couple of weeks to create a single town RPG. Months for a more expansive world.

The way it works is you describe your world in plain English - rules, the feel, how characters and objects interact. The engine reads that and drafts a blueprint. You review it before it generates anything. If it got your idea wrong, you tell it. You look again -  over and over until it is precisely what you wanted. Your story. Your game. The way you wanted it to be.  
  
I am at the stage I can get a single prompt to create the blueprint, make some corrections and answer clarifying questions. But there is still a lot of work left. I’m hoping to get the demo ready in the next couple of weeks.  
  
Let me know if you are interested in seeing it when I am ready.

replies.author: Sure_Excuse_8824
replies.body:
Sounds awesome.   
As a novelist who enjoys games, it wasn't hard to see how the really great games were mostly about the story. What is Halo without the Master Chief, the Covenant, and the Flood? Just a cool shooter. What is Final Fantasy, Tales of, and others without the story behind them? 

I know a lot of writers who would love to bring their stories to life in a game. That was the inspiration for the design.

comments.author: Old-Preference5313
comments.body: Even the best ai models struggle to make games, what makes your prompts / ai bettter? Assuming you will just route it through Claude or codex right? Probably need to wait for the the technology to get better before you can make this a reality

replies.author: Sure_Excuse_8824
replies.body:
Everyone who waits for a smarter model is waiting for a better liar. My intended design is the opposite. AI is never the creator. That's human. It proposes. A compiler only admits what the engine can actually run. Suppose you have a fantasy village, and your prompt is "the blacksmith is in the assassin guild"  that sticks. Magic boxes fail because they are the AI with a wrapper.

Just a Game Engine is the pipeline that refuses to let the AI finish the sentence.

replies.author: Ok-Investment4414
replies.body:
idk if OP can pull it off but if he fine tunes a model like qwen 3.8 - 27b it likely would out perform claude / gpt  frontiers without massive context . Thats assuming he got a frontier model distilled for the responses and gets something like a rag setup to draw extra context.   
And you would be surprized :-/ this is def redflag lawsuit territory but ingest a few Dnd crafting books along with powerusers in discord , reddit , forums , facebook etc comments and feed back (those multi paragraphs posters writing a short novel as a reply) and you have a real system on your hands.

replies.author: Sure_Excuse_8824
replies.body:
Yup! I’ve gone down that rabbit hole. A fine-tuned local 27B would crush a frontier model for this job if trained right. Honestly though, getting better ideas from the AI isn't really my biggest bottleneck right now. Claude and Qwen do a good job with suggestions. The gap I am trying to cross is what happens after the suggestions are given. Most tools just accept whatever the AI spits out, but I build mine to stop, review, and verify. Getting that core loop right is more important to me than a smarter brain.

I love the D&D corpus idea.  I’m not sure about the legal end though. My focus has been solving the engineering challenges. It’s already clear at some point I’ll need to recruit some other people who think it’s worthwhile. But that’s something I can deal with later. For now I still have my head above water.

The local model issue is the thing I keep coming back to, though. For the breed of storytellers I'm building this for, knowing their world never leaves their own hard drive is very important. We’ve already received all the money we’ll likely see from AI companies for the crap they pulled.
